short: The final and most formidable attempt by the Jacobites to overthrow the British monarchy.
full:
In August 1745, Prince Charles Edward Stuart launched a bold insurrection in Scotland to restore his family to the British throne. Without the promised French military support, he rallied Highland clans and achieved rapid early victories, decisively defeating government forces at Prestonpans. The Jacobite army then invaded England, reaching Derby by December and causing panic in London.

Lacking English support and facing larger government armies, the Jacobite leaders controversially ordered a retreat back to Scotland. Despite winning another tactical victory at Falkirk Muir, they were eventually cornered and annihilated at the Battle of Culloden in April 1746. The defeat marked the definitive end of Jacobitism as a serious political or military threat.
